correctness.rationale: With b>0, mark a transition and record ordered pairs of alternating positive run lengths; a necklace corresponds to one orbit under simultaneous rotation of the b pairs. A rotation of order ell fixes precisely the ell-fold repetitions, giving the stated divisor sum by stars and bars. Its nonidentity terms total at most 2^(n/2) since the totients for all ell dividing b sum to b. Writing r=a+b, s=d+b gives the identity term as 2^n b p_r(b)p_s(b)/(rs). The entropy exponent is continuous on the closed feasible triangle, including zero-weight endpoints, and reaches one only at a=b=d=n/4. Thus a balanced lower witness excludes maximizers outside any fixed fractional neighborhood. Near the peak, Stirling at b-r/2=(b-a)/2 and b-s/2=(b-d)/2 gives the stated exponent and 4/pi prefactor uniformly, including odd r or s. For a global upper bound, fractional balance already suffices: use the maximum point masses of each fair binomial, without assuming that a maximizing triple lies in a square-root window. Constant necklaces contribute one to their separate fibers and do not compete asymptotically.
residual_risks: The finite checker does not prove the infinite limit or independently attest the arithmetic maxima outside its exhaustive lengths 1–15. In particular it does not test every length 16–160 despite the verification note's phrasing.

originality.rationale: A distinct November 2 catalogue statement gives precisely the indexed binary cyclic pair-count maximum asymptotic to (4/pi)2^n/n, and more strongly classifies its finite maximizing profiles. For each profile F/n differs from the necklace count by at most the total number of nonprimitive necklaces, at most n 2^(n/2), because each primitive necklace has n indexed representatives and each other necklace has a period at most n/2. This comparison is uniform and transfers the earlier sharp global limit with exactly the same constant. The local profile is not claimed to be verbatim in that entry: it is ordinary central Stirling applied to the two binomial factors of the exact indexed count F=(nb/(rs)) binom(r,b) binom(s,b), followed by the same uniform correction. That count follows by distinguishing one transition at one of n indices and dividing by b; it is the classical transition-total ingredient acknowledged in the record. Thus changing the equivalence relation does not establish a new sharp maximum, and the local display has no separate nonstandard limit or counting ingredient.
residual_risks: Verbatim prior local Gaussian coverage and the full Whittle passage are unresolved. The central global result is demonstrably implied by the earlier indexed statement and a uniform elementary inequality; the decision is not based on missing sources.
